method: Subscribed to the live guided-objective store and UX feedback bus through the Vite ESM graph, so every publish, marker-health change and objective-enter cue is counted at emit time. Counts aggregate three ch7 cold movie runs, three ch8 cold movie runs, six variant runs (mobile portrait, reduced motion, POTATO across both beats) and the reset traces.
runtimeIdMapping: The scene contract uses hyphenated guidance IDs; the runtime publishes colon-separated IDs. reconstruct-diagnose = reconstruct:diagnose, reconstruct-repair-bench-online = reconstruct:repair:bench_online, reconstruct-repair-frame-restored = reconstruct:repair:frame_restored, reconstruct-repair-hull-sealed = reconstruct:repair:hull_sealed, reconstruct-craft-lift-online = reconstruct:craft:lift_online, reconstruct-repair-lift-online = reconstruct:repair:lift_online, reconstruct-craft-flight-ready = reconstruct:craft:flight_ready, reconstruct-repair-flight-ready = reconstruct:repair:flight_ready, ch8-launch-reboard = ch8:launch:reboard.
markerHealthDefinition: missingMarkerFrames below counts store observations in which the objective was active with health 'missing-marker'. Each entry produces two such observations by construction: one at publish (before the marker driver has run) and one at replacement (after the driver drops the outgoing target). The measured duration of that transient is 0.000-0.001 s for every objective except reconstruct:diagnose at beat entry, where it is the shipped 2.956-3.137 s marker-resolution window recorded as baseline limitation 5. No new missing-marker state is introduced by this run.
undisturbedSummary: No objective was added, renamed, re-copied or re-marked by this run. Every observed marker label, work order, kind and requiresMarker value is byte-identical to the signed guidance contract and to the shipped baseline trace, and objective-enter feedback fired exactly once per entry on every path and every variant. npm --prefix main run story:ux:check re-ran green post-implementation (6 files, 54 tests).

knownPreExistingDefectUnchanged.observation: The objective covers two player actions (claim salvage, then install the keel workbench) under one ID, so the HUD keeps showing 'WRECK BENCH · RECOVER WRECK SALVAGE' / '[F] RECOVER WRECK SALVAGE.' while the required action becomes '[F] INSTALL KEEL WORKBENCH'. Measured unchanged after implementation: the label observed on all six entries is exactly 'WRECK BENCH · RECOVER WRECK SALVAGE' and the work order is exactly the two shipped lines. This run neither repaired nor worsened it.

restoredScreenLife.note: Not a guidance.objectives entry (requiresMarker false, so the contract carries it as an acceptance term). Recorded here because variant D's restored screen life is a contract obligation.
restoredScreenLife.baselineComparison: The shipped baseline trace never sampled this objective at all, consistent with its recorded unreachability (shipped-reference-map defect 3).

nonMarkerObjectivesUndisturbed.note: Did not publish on the POTATO tier run (ignite went straight to orbital-handoff). No POTATO baseline exists for comparison.
Publish restored by the R2 hold; ID, work order and requiresMarker value all unchanged.

workOrder: AIM AT THE SCAR. [F] TRACE RELATIONSHIPS.
objectives.markerHealthAccounting: Per-requestAnimationFrame sample of getGuidedStoryObjectiveHealth() alongside the active objective. preAcquisitionMissingMarkerFrames are frames before the marker ever resolved for that activation (acceptance criterion [35] records this entry acquisition transient as an accepted measured exception). clearFrameMissingMarkerFrames is the single trailing frame on which the marker target is consumed and the objective is replaced in the same tick. missingMarkerFrames is what remains: frames while the objective was active, already acquired, and not yet clearing. The three add up to every measured missing-marker frame; nothing is discarded.
